title: 7-Year Treasury Note auction — the day before Thanksgiving, closing 11:30am ET not 1:00pm
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-19 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 rows. Row reads `7-Year NOTE / Announcement Thursday, November 19, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, November 25, 2026 / Settlement Monday, November 30, 2026`, with NO trailing `R` marker — a new issue, as every 7-Year has been. The AUCTION TIME is sourced rather than assumed: fiscaldata auctions_query publishes `closing_time_comp`, which reads `11:30 AM` on all SIX pre-Thanksgiving 7-Year auctions in the record (2014-11-26, 2015-11-25, 2016-11-23, 2019-11-27, 2024-11-27, 2025-11-26) against `01:00 PM` on 143 of the other 146, so 2026-11-25 should be read as an 11:30am ET close. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-11-19 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-19 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed because its proposer is the announcement that sizes it. THE WEEKDAY IS A HOLIDAY DISPLACEMENT, measured: in the tentative schedule's Aug-2026-to-Jan-2027 window the 7-Year auctions on a THURSDAY in 4 of 6 months (08-27, 09-24, 10-29, 2027-01-28); the two exceptions are November (Wednesday, Thanksgiving) and December (Tuesday, year-end). SIZE EXPECTATION $44B, unchanged at every 7-Year auction since 2024-04-25 and identical in all six monthly rows sb0590 publishes (May-26 through Oct-26 all read 44) — the 7-Year sits in the INVARIANT columns of that table because it is a new issue every month, so no new-issue/reopening cycle has to be read correctly. THE TEMPTING STORY IS MEASURED AND IT IS A NULL, which is why this is worth tracking rather than assuming: a 7-Year selling into a thinned pre-holiday session with an early close LOOKS like a demand problem and is not. Across all 152 7-Year auctions since 2014, the six pre-Thanksgiving ones averaged bid-to-cover 2.572 against 2.490 for the other 146 and 2.556 for the 2024-05-onward regime alone; indirect share 61.4% vs 62.3%. The two most recent (2024-11-27 b/c 2.71, 2025-11-26 b/c 2.46) bracket the pool mean rather than sitting under it. That null is pre-registered as FT-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-19-2, which predicts b/c >= 2.40 here — no 7-Year auction since 2024-05 has printed below 2.40 (28 of 28), and 2026's eight prints run 2.43 to 2.52. SESSION CONTEXT, and the honest reason no clean attribution will be possible: 2026-11-25 is the densest macro session of the month, everything having been pulled forward off the Thanksgiving closure — pce-2026-11-25 and gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25 at 8:30am ET, durable-goods-2026-11-25 and new-home-sales-2026-11-25, beige-book-2026-11-25 at 2:00pm, plus the 4-week, 8-week and 17-week bill auctions and the 13/26-week announcement all displaced onto the same Wednesday. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
